analysis: Examined the three changed files. In StatusCommand.swift (head lines 168 and 191-193), `darkbloom status` now also prints `pendingSelectionLines` and `recoveryLines`, in addition to the existing `selectionLines` and `evictionExclusionLines`. These are local, read-only diagnostics derived from the owner-readable daemon state file (`DaemonStateFile.read()`) and the saved config. No network, key, attestation, authorization or coordinator-facing code path is touched. The helpers `pendingSelectionLines` and `recoveryLines` are defined elsewhere and were not supplied, so their contents were not reviewed. They render fields such as selected-model recovery `blocker`, `enabled_models_at_start` and `enabled_models_at_last_switch`. The blocker string holds model IDs and memory figures from the daemon's own state, and I see no prompts or A-001 data in the fields shown. A local operator who edits the state file could only alter their own CLI output, which is not a privilege boundary here. The other two files are test-only. StatusResidencyTests.swift adds sandboxed child-process tests that use a temporary provider home. AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift adds two test-only setters for `autopilotResidentSince` and `autopilotLeaseUntil` in a `@testable` extension, which do not ship in production. No threat-model assets (A-001 to A-019), boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 and TB-012 among them) or mitigations appear changed. Residual question: the unseen `pendingSelectionLines` and `recoveryLines` implementations should print only non-sensitive daemon state. Nothing in the supplied evidence suggests they print anything else, so I raise no finding.
